prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins, through PROTACs and the mechanism of molecular glues.

statement.case_for: Reading all eight openings, B020 is the only candidate that seven of eight members place in their top three, and I no longer think that convergence is only a matter of taste. The chemical idea is sharp and general: a small molecule that forms a ternary complex with an E3 ligase and a target, giving event-driven, catalytic removal of the protein instead of occupancy-based inhibition. The mechanism is supported by structures and kinetics of ternary complexes and by cooperativity measurements, and it has been reproduced by many groups. The cereblon strand explains, after the fact, how thalidomide-type drugs work, so the glue and the heterobifunctional strands share a mechanistic basis. That lets a single citation describe an actual principle and not a list of compounds. I ranked B028 first on scientific grounds close to my own field, and I still think nitrogenase deserves a prize, but I have to be honest that no colleague ranked it and that my own attribution problem there (Rees, Dean, Seefeldt, Einsle, Ribbe, plus Burgess and Hoffman who are not even on the list) is harder than for B020. For this round the strongest, best-defined proposal is B020 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC drug is approved, so recognition rests on concept and mechanism rather than clinical proof, and a prize in a young modality risks being early if the clinical results disappoint. The three-person limit also excludes Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito, each with a defensible claim, and the PROTAC and glue lineages are historically separate, so the combined citation may look like a forced merger. There is also a fair worry that this is a medicinal chemistry and pharmacology achievement that a Medicine committee could just as readily claim.

responses.point: Aili ranks B020 first but proposes Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, treating the cereblon glue strand (Handa, Ito) as a separate lineage that the three-person limit may exclude.
responses.response: I take the point that Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and his work on ternary-complex design are a real chemical contribution, and that the glue lineage has a different history. But I would still put Handa in the third slot. Without the identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target, the glue half of the field has no mechanism, and it is the part that is already in patients. Ciulli's work builds on and extends the Crews and Deshaies concept, while Handa's is an independent discovery. I accept that this leaves Ciulli out and that the choice is contestable, and I would not oppose a configuration with him if the committee judges design principles to outweigh the target discovery.

responses.point: Linke, the chair, ranks B020 first with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, calling it a conceptually original, chemically general modality whose weakness is that it may be slightly early.
responses.response: I agree with the attribution and with the view that the concept is more settled than the clinical record. Where I would qualify his view is on timing. Lenalidomide-class glues are already established drugs, and the mechanism of cereblon recruitment is confirmed structurally, so the part of the field that is early is PROTACs, not the principle. I would therefore not make the prize wait for a PROTAC approval, and the citation should be worded around the mechanism.

responses.point: Chabes ranks base editing B047 first, arguing that deaminase chemistry on a single-stranded R-loop is a clean, clinically used molecular tool, with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli as a coherent trio.
responses.response: I find the chemistry persuasive and I ranked it fourth. My reservation is not about the science but about the framing after the 2020 prize and about naming the trainees. Naming Komor and Gaudelli next to Liu is a judgment that the committee has to make openly, since Kondo and Nishida reported a parallel approach. Compared with B020, base editing has less breadth of mechanism and, for now, fewer patients treated. I would keep it as my second alternative rather than as the lead, but I do not dismiss it and could support it if B020 stalls on attribution.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics first, citing unusually clean two-person attribution and four decades of confirmed impact, so recognition is overdue rather than premature.
responses.response: I agree that the credit is clean and that Car and Parrinello is a strong, mature candidate. It is the best case on attribution on the list. My hesitation is only about how much of the chemistry community's current activity it represents compared with a new modality, and about computational recognition in 2013 and 2024. I would not oppose it if it can be put into a two-part prize, but it was not in my own top eight, and I would need to hear how its influence on experimental chemistry compares with that of B020.

responses.point: Somfai ranks B020 only fourth and considers it somewhat premature because clinical validation is still emerging, preferring the mature C-N coupling candidate B044.
responses.response: The prematurity concern is the most serious one against B020, and I do not dismiss it. But C-N coupling was ranked in the top eight by only two members, and the 2010 prize for cross-coupling makes it harder to argue novelty. Hartwig is also proposed in B008, which complicates the picture. My view is that conceptual and mechanistic maturity, confirmed by many independent groups and by structures, is what the Nobel criterion asks for, and the clinical proof is not required in the same way as for a drug prize.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept Handa over Ciulli, or Ciulli over Crews, for the third place.
Whether B020 is judged too early without an approved PROTAC drug, and whether a one-year delay would change the picture.
Whether the PROTAC and glue strands should be one citation or two prize parts.
I am relying on memory for exact priority dates of the 2001 PROTAC paper and the 2010 cereblon work and have not checked them.
How to treat nitrogenase (B028) given that Burgess and Hoffman are not among the credited names.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for any shortlisted candidate. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, but she ranks B007, which is not my preference, and I have no stated link to the candidates in B020, B028 or B047. My own field (respiratory proton transfer) is close to B028, which I disclose as a possible bias.
